evidence_unit.source_title: Revealing the Dark Side of Smart Accounts: An Empirical Study of EIP-7702 Incurred Risks in Blockchain Ecosystem
evidence_unit.method: Large-scale transaction analysis plus cross-contract static analysis across seven EIP-7702-supporting blockchains.
evidence_unit.population: EIP-7702 authorization transactions analyzed across seven supported blockchains in the published study.
evidence_unit.supported_claim: Account-abstraction convenience changes the trust boundary and makes authorization/revocation controls a first-class architecture decision.
evidence_unit.boundary: This evidence is specific to the study dataset and EIP-7702 ecosystem. It does not establish a universal compromise probability for account abstraction or all smart-account designs.
evidence_unit.blocker: The NeoFort source object is verified but lacks the proof-carrying materialized origin artifact/content hash required by the current deterministic preflight policy. Do not admit or publish until materialized and re-judged.

question_driven_graph_evidence_unit.question: What measurable European market conditions justify architecture qualification before selecting a tokenisation or DLT mechanism?
question_driven_graph_evidence_unit.source_title: From vision to delivery: building Europe’s tokenised financial market

panel.population: European market infrastructure cited by the ECB
panel.boundary: Counts describe current market structure; they do not prove DLT removes fragmentation.

panel.population: transactions by volume/value in the ECB-cited European CSD context
panel.boundary: Same-CSD settlement shares measure locality/fragmentation, not ledger performance.

panel.population: Eurosystem exploratory DLT work cited by the ECB
panel.boundary: Participation and experiments show activity, not production adoption or economic benefit.

panel.population: tokenised traditional assets on public blockchains in the ECB source scope
panel.boundary: Two market-value observations provide context only; no causal or forecast claim is permitted.

question_driven_graph_evidence_unit.graph_interpretation: The evidence supports a qualification thesis: Europe combines fragmented infrastructure, active experimentation and a rapidly larger but still bounded tokenised-asset base. These facts justify deciding the verifier, coordination problem and acceptance condition before choosing DLT. They do not prove that DLT is superior for a specific workload.
question_driven_graph_evidence_unit.blocker: The current NeoFort ECB source record is verified but not proof-carrying/materialized with the source snapshot identity required for a new admitted QG-EU. Keep this graph as a proposed specification until materialization, observation-level provenance and all applicable judge snapshots pass.

replacement.target_xpath: //main//h1[normalize-space(.)="Ancrez on-chain ce qu’un tiers doit vérifier, jamais ce qu’il suffit de stocker."]
replacement.before: Ancrez on-chain ce qu’un tiers doit vérifier, jamais ce qu’il suffit de stocker.
replacement.after: Make the property verifiable. Keep the system as simple as the property allows.
replacement.reason: Preserves the property-first category while removing an unnecessary presumption that the proof must be on-chain.

replacement.after: Define what a third party must verify before selecting the mechanism. Use controlled database evidence when one operator can legitimately own the state; add attestations, smart contracts or selective proofs only when independent verification or shared execution justifies the machinery.[1]
replacement.boundary: Database throughput and multi-party coordination are separate decision dimensions.

replacement.target_xpath: //*[contains(normalize-space(.), "Le projet démarre par une plateforme")][not(.//*[contains(normalize-space(.), "Le projet démarre par une plateforme")])]
replacement.after: If an audited database satisfies the verifier, authority, integrity and disclosure requirements, stop there. Add ledger machinery only for a verification or coordination property that the simpler architecture cannot satisfy.[2]
replacement.boundary: Do not claim universal cost savings or universal database superiority.

replacement.target_xpath: //main//*[self::p or self::div][contains(normalize-space(.),"Qui signe, qui révoque") and contains(normalize-space(.),"perte ou de départ")]
replacement.after: Define who can authorize, revoke, recover and escalate before deployment. Account abstraction can improve usability while changing the trust boundary; recent EIP-7702 evidence shows why authorization policy must be treated as an architecture control, not a wallet detail.[3]

replacement.target_xpath: //main//*[self::p or self::div][contains(normalize-space(.),"La plupart des projets blockchain paient pour stocker") and contains(normalize-space(.),"frontière claim/evidence")]
replacement.after: Start from the verifier, the property, the disclosure boundary and the authority model. Then choose the minimum mechanism that closes that verification gap: controlled evidence, append-only records, attestations, smart contracts, identity controls or selective/ZK proofs. A documented no-blockchain decision is a valid paid outcome.
replacement.reason: Removes the unsupported universal “most blockchain projects” claim while retaining the differentiated architecture method.

replacement.target_xpath: //main//*[self::p or self::div][contains(normalize-space(.),"La preuve va on-chain") and contains(normalize-space(.),"donnée confidentielle reste off-chain")]
replacement.after: Separate what must be proven from what must be revealed. Keep protected inputs outside the verifier’s disclosure boundary whenever the acceptance condition can be established from a bounded commitment, attestation or proof.
replacement.boundary: This is an architecture rule, not a claim that every proof belongs on-chain.

replacement.after: Public contribution evidence: 26 of 29 repository commits are attributed to RickOwri for the Lottery dApp fork; this demonstrates substantial implementation work without claiming original authorship of the starter project.
replacement.reason: Commit attribution is evidence of contribution, not a defensible percentage of product development.
